reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a tutorial about earning as a student through Course Hero tutoring and shows ordinary account-registration and tutor-application steps. The earning claim and registration link are risk-relevant, but the described evidence does not establish a guaranteed amount, payment occurrence, deceptive demand, credential theft, fabricated transaction, or misrepresentation of the signup form.

citations.quote: I'm going to talk to you guys about how you can make a thousand rupees every day very easily.
And if you become a tutor here, you become an educator.
You have to create your own frees account here.
when you register here, you have to select the field you want to solve the question.

opening.argument: The video presents a simple income proposition and directly connects it to participation on Course Hero. Its title promises daily earnings while studying, while the narration says viewers can earn that amount and directs them toward becoming a tutor, creating an account, and selecting a field. That is a reward linked to concrete viewer actions, not merely general education. The signup page shown also combines tutor enrollment with an earning-related activity, reinforcing that viewers are being led from the promise toward registration.

citations.quote: Earn ₹ 1,000 Daily While Studying
you can make a thousand rupees every day very easily
And if you become a tutor here, you become an educator.
You have to create your own frees account here.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the process an ordinary account registration does not answer the central issue: registration is presented as the route to the advertised daily income. The defense also omits that the narration couples becoming a tutor with the earning claim and then instructs viewers to create an account and choose a field. A routine-looking form can still be the action demanded by a low-barrier income solicitation.

citations.quote: you can make a thousand rupees every day very easily
when you register here, you have to select the field you want to solve the question

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted material shows an advertised possibility and an application route, but it does not show that registration itself produces money. The account and field-selection instructions are consistent with applying to perform tutoring work, and the evidence does not establish payment, guaranteed earnings, or a deceptive requirement. The relationship between application and income therefore remains an ordinary work opportunity rather than proof of a scam.

citations.quote: And if you become a tutor here, you become an educator.
when you register here, you have to select the field you want to solve the question

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: the title advertises ₹1,000 every day, the narration characterizes that income as very easy, and the description supplies direct Telegram and Course Hero links. The displayed tutor page places an earning-related activity beside a form requesting an email address, username, and password. That combination lowers the apparent barrier to cash while moving viewers toward an external signup, making the offer materially more suspicious than a neutral explanation of tutoring.

citations.quote: Earn ₹ 1,000 Daily While Studying
you can make a thousand rupees every day very easily
Telegram Channel https://telegram.im/@theengineerguychannel
Website: https://www.coursehero.com/register/?become_tutor=1

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each signal in isolation. It acknowledges the earning claim and link but discounts their combination with the ease language and the signup form. A branded-looking page does not validate the promised return, and an educational presentation can still be used to make a low-effort income pitch appear safe. The evidence supports concern about the solicitation even without a fabricated transaction.

citations.quote: Earn ₹ 1,000 Daily While Studying
very easily

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals establish only that the video advertises tutoring income and provides a way to apply. The supplied evidence does not show that the amount is guaranteed, that applicants must pay, or that the credentials are collected for an improper purpose. The visible form and links are compatible with a legitimate tutor application, so suspicion from presentation style cannot substitute for evidence of deception.

citations.quote: if you become a tutor here, you become an educator.
if you have to learn how to register, you have to comment once and I'll tell you.

opening.argument: Although framed as help for students, the content functions as promotion for a specific participation pathway. It names Course Hero, directs viewers to a tutor-registration page, explains that they should create an account and select a field, and pairs those steps with an easy daily-income message. The educational framing therefore makes the solicitation more persuasive: viewers are encouraged to see enrollment as a practical study aid and income shortcut rather than critically evaluating whether the advertised return is substantiated.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense focuses on the mechanics of tutoring and overlooks the promotional framing. The video is not merely demonstrating how to solve an academic question; it uses that instructional setting to direct students toward a named platform and account creation while advertising easy income. Describing the steps as ordinary does not remove their role in steering viewers into the promoted service.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A recommendation or tutorial about a named service is not by itself deceptive promotion. The evidence describes tutoring-related tasks and an application process, including selecting a subject to solve, but it does not show concealed sponsorship, false credentials, or an outcome obtained merely by signing up. The promotional interpretation adds intent and deception that the supplied material does not establish.
